sonnet.q1: They do not differ. Both get 401 with the login page and 'Invalid email or password' (an unknown email runs bcrypt against a dummy hash so timing matches too).
sonnet.q2: The fifth failure sets a lock key (15-minute TTL) and clears the fails key. The next attempt checks the lock (PTTL) at step 2 and gets 429 with Retry-After (the remaining milliseconds rounded up to whole seconds). The database is not read and the password is not checked.
sonnet.q3: On a successful login, the Redis transaction deletes the old session (if a sid was sent) and creates a new session under a new random ID. The new cookie ID replaces the old one, which blocks session fixation.
sonnet.q4: Only the random session ID (sid, 32 random bytes base64url, 43 chars) travels in the cookie. No user data goes in it. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It is also Secure, SameSite=Lax and Path=/, with no Max-Age.
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after login (absolute expiry). Each request extends the idle timer to the smaller of 30 minutes and the time left, so the key expires exactly at 12 hours. After that the request gets 302 to /login.
sonnet.q6: If the sess key is missing (unknown or expired), it returns 302 to /login and clears the sid cookie. If the record is found but absolute_expires_at has passed, it deletes the key and gives the same 302 with the cookie cleared.
sonnet.q7: If a sid cookie is present, the server deletes the sess key for the hash of sid. Then it returns 303 to /login with the cookie cleared. A key that is already gone counts as success, and the reply is the same. With no cookie it skips the delete and sends the same reply. If the DEL errors, it returns 503 and keeps the cookie.
sonnet.q8: In Redis, a shared store that both app copies can read. The browser sends the sid cookie. The instance hashes it with SHA-256 and reads the key sess: plus that hash from Redis.
sonnet.q9: In Redis, in a sorted set under the key fails: plus the hash of the email. It holds the times of recent failed logins. On each failure a Lua script removes entries older than 10 minutes, adds this attempt, and counts what is left.
sonnet.q10: It compares the current UTC time with absolute_expires_at from the session record. If the session is still valid, it writes back an EXPIRE on the sess key, setting the TTL to the smaller of 30 minutes and the time left until absolute_expires_at.
sonnet.q11: A 503 with 'Sign-in is unavailable right now. Try again in a few minutes.' and no cookie. This holds when the MULTI/EXEC transaction fails.
sonnet.q12: Redis does, by itself. It deletes a key when its TTL passes. No sweeper or cleanup job is needed. Sessions found to be expired or logged out are also deleted at that moment.
